root_cause.text: The fst_remove_one() function deallocates the fst_card_info structure via kfree(card) without first canceling the global tasklets fst_tx_task and fst_int_task, which may still be pending or executing and will access the freed card structure in their handlers fst_process_tx_work_q() and fst_process_int_work_q().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds tasklet_kill(&fst_tx_task) and tasklet_kill(&fst_int_task) calls in fst_remove_one() after fst_disable_intr() and free_irq() but before the card structure is freed. The KASAN trace shows do_bottom_half_tx() accessing the freed card object at address ffff88800aad101c after kfree(card) is called in fst_remove_one(), demonstrating that the global tasklets were not properly synchronized before deallocation. The race condition occurs because tasklet_schedule() can queue these global tasklets during device operation, but fst_remove_one() previously freed the card without ensuring these tasklets had completed execution.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure tasklets are killed before device removal to prevent use-after-free bugs from tasklet execution after interrupt handler deregistration.
intent_record.what: Added two tasklet_kill() calls for fst_tx_task and fst_int_task after the free_irq() call in the fst_remove_one() function.
intent_record.how: These calls ensure that any pending tasklets are stopped and cleaned up before the device is fully removed. This prevents tasklets from executing after their associated interrupt handler has been freed, which could cause use-after-free or null pointer dereference bugs if tasklets try to access freed device memory.

bic_trace_step.reason: The fst_remove_one() function (starting at line ~2650) deallocates the fst_card_info structure via kfree(card) at the end without first canceling the global tasklets fst_tx_task and fst_int_task. These tasklets are declared globally (DECLARE_TASKLET lines ~1100-1101) and their handlers fst_process_tx_work_q() and fst_process_int_work_q() access card structures from the fst_card_array. The function calls fst_disable_intr(card) and free_irq(card->irq, card) but never calls tasklet_kill() or tasklet_disable() on fst_tx_task or fst_int_task. This means if these tasklets are pending or executing when fst_remove_one() deallocates the card structure via kfree(card), they will access freed memory when they try to access fst_card_array[i] in their handlers (lines ~1130-1135 and ~1150-1155). The vulnerability is present because: (1) the vulnerable construct (missing tasklet cancellation before kfree) IS present, and (2) the code does NOT have the correct handling to prevent the vulnerability.
